generated_at: reproducible deterministic computation; no network access
limitations: One small study window/site; 1024 spatially autocorrelated sample locations are not independent events.
NISAR has six acquisitions; C-band dates do not create additional independent NISAR temporal observations.
L- and C-band polarization channels are not equivalent; frequency effects cannot be isolated from polarization, orbit, incidence geometry, resolution, processor and date.

RTC points have no per-point contributing-granule receipt or saved per-point quality/geometry mask; a date can combine bursts/versions in first-valid order. Granule-level UTC timestamp ranges cannot establish each point's actual lag or geometry.
Date matching uses calendar dates; UTC granule timestamps are separately recorded, but no per-point timestamp exists for the selected RTC value.
Difference between class/date medians is not treated as the median of paired pointwise differences; change correlations are computed from paired pointwise differences.
WorldCover 2021 is historical; class-30 grassland is not verified pasture.
No independent event labels; do not infer clearing, event detection accuracy, causation or wavelength superiority.
Monthly C-band medians pool years and can confound season with trend, orbit/track or acquisition geometry; not a fitted seasonal decomposition.

acquisition_times.nisar: UTC start times from data/subsets/amazon-dense/<date>.json source metadata; these sidecars identify the same acquisition granules in the series.
acquisition_times.opera: UTC acquisition timestamp parsed from each granule ID; all per-date burst granules included
acquisition_times.precision: Granule-level UTC timestamps are available, but actual per-point contributing burst is unknown; exact per-point lag is therefore unavailable.

coordinates.assertions: AMA row/column ID, grid-derived cell-center lat/lon, 1024 array length, and ordered coordinate hash.
coordinates.matching: Validated each NISAR ID and lat/lon against declared 32x32 grid; verified ordered lat/lon SHA-256 equals OPERA points_sha256. OPERA coordinates/IDs are not stored per point; order contract is required.

metadata.masks: Analysis only requires finite, shared point values; no additional per-point geometry/quality mask can be applied from the stored RTC JSON.
metadata.nisar_collection: NISAR L2 GCOV PROVISIONAL; track 146/frame 175 ascending per data/amazon-manifest.json
metadata.opera_orbit_track_metadata: per-granule orbit/track not in sidecar; not inferred; granule IDs retained for matched dates

radiometry.nisar: GCOV gamma0, HH/HV, positive power to 10log10, source masks 0/255 rejected during extraction; only stored valid/null values consumed here.
radiometry.opera: RTC-S1 gamma0 VV/VH dB, per scripts/opera_rtc.py uses VV/VH assets and 10log10(linear power); no sigma0 auxiliary used.
radiometry.quality: No saved per-point RTC quality mask or contributing burst; finite values are not equivalent to verified quality/geometry.

bootstrap.contrast_seed_rule: base seed + block size; identical block draw used for level/change correlation within each replicate
bootstrap.unit: spatial blocks; paired coordinates and dates, not independent pixels

method.change: per-coordinate consecutive differences over successive matched pairs; changes overlap in coordinates and temporal intervals; temporal sample size is number of dates, not point-date rows.
method.level_correlation: pooled point-date observations; centered by WorldCover class AND acquisition-date median within each sensor before spatial correlation.
method.matching: Nearest calendar date per NISAR acquisition, with unique RTC date assignments for tolerance analyses; ID+lat/lon grid and ordered hash checks; no interpolation; primary tolerance 6 days. UTC granule ranges are reported separately, not assigned to pixels.

study: Amazon NISAR L-band vs OPERA Sentinel-1 C-band; spatial/temporal association and class confounding
